slot.brief: Give a snapshot graph (y vs x at t=0) of a sinusoidal wave; ask to read amplitude, wavelength and then frequency/wave speed from the standard wave equation matched to the diagram.

stem: A sinusoidal wave travelling along the positive x-direction is shown at t = 0 in the figure. The wave speed is 24 m s^-1. The frequency of the wave is:

verdicts.working: The graph shows one complete wavelength over 6 m, so \(\lambda=6\,\text{m}\). Thus \(f=v/\lambda=24/6=4\,\text{Hz}\).

working:
From the figure, one complete cycle runs from x = 0 to x = 6 m, so the wavelength is lambda = 6 m.
Given wave speed v = 24 m s^-1.
Frequency f = v / lambda = 24 / 6 = 4 Hz.
Thus the correct option is B.

Independent check: The graph shows one complete wavelength over 6 m, so \(\lambda=6\,\text{m}\). Thus \(f=v/\lambda=24/6=4\,\text{Hz}\).
solution: From the figure, one complete cycle spans $\lambda=6\,\text{m}$. Using $v=f\lambda$, $$f=\frac{v}{\lambda}=\frac{24}{6}=4\,\text{Hz}.$$
